title: Fourth moment bound under slice hypotheses
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $d,e:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and $f:\{-1,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. Suppose that $f(b,x)=bd(x)+e(x)$ for every $b\in\{-1,1\}$ and $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. Let $A,B\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0\le A$ and $0\le B$, and suppose that $\mathbb E[d^4]\le A^2/9$ and $\mathbb E[e^4]\le B^2$, with expectations uniform on the respective cubes. Then $\mathbb E[f^4]\le(A+B)^2$, with expectation uniform on the $(n+1)$-dimensional cube.
hypotheses_covered: $d$ and $e$ are real-valued functions on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube
For every first-coordinate sign and remaining input, $f(b,x)=bd(x)+e(x)$
